meta.license: U.S. government data. The Department's pages state no terms of use; a Data.gov catalog record lists the data as public with a CC0 license, which is not the Department's own statement. Cite the Department of Education and NCES as the sources. To be confirmed by the Northeastern library before this goes public.
meta.geography: One record per campus of each institution in the United States and its territories, located by the institution's address and, on the map, by its main location in the IPEDS directory (not by campus). Places inside a campus are the Clery places: on campus, residence halls, noncampus buildings, public property. No tract, county or neighborhood figures are made from these counts. Campuses abroad are left out.
meta.notice: Source: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Postsecondary Education, Campus Safety and Security data (Clery Act crime statistics), collections 2008 to 2025; locations from the National Center for Education Statistics, IPEDS Institutional Characteristics (HD) file. Counts are crimes reported to campus officials and local police, as each institution counted and submitted them. They are not all crime, not victimization, and not comparable between schools.
limits: Counts of crimes reported to campus security, campus officials and police in the calendar year, as each school counted them. They are not all crime and not victimization: many crimes are never reported.
Schools are not comparable: what is reported depends on reporting practices, campus definition, housing, the police around it and the culture of reporting. A higher count can mean more reporting.
Administrative records of nearly every participating school, not a sample: there are no weights, no sampling error and no margin of error. That does not mean the counts are exact.
Small counts swing year to year on one or two reports. A blank is "no figure" and a 0 is "reported none"; the two are kept apart.

Definitions changed: sex offenses are forcible and nonforcible through 2013 and rape, fondling, incest and statutory rape from 2014; VAWA offenses, unfounded crimes and hate-crime detail were added later. Do not chain across a break.
Residence halls are part of on campus: never add them. Hate crimes are shown beside, not added to, criminal offenses.
Institution totals add the U.S. campuses only. The Department screens add campuses abroad too, so a school with a campus abroad can show a smaller number here than there.
Enrollment is one institution-wide figure per report, so rates are shown for the institution, not for a campus.
A campus is followed by its institution and branch number; a school that closed, merged or changed its id has a cut-off or separate series.
